question: Most of the iron in human blood was made in which kind of stellar death?
options: A white dwarf blowing itself apart
A red giant shedding its layers
answer: A white dwarf blowing itself apart. A collapsing giant never releases its iron core; it is crushed into a neutron star or black hole. Exploding white dwarfs, each forging about half a Sun's mass of iron, made about two-thirds of the Solar System's supply. Blood's iron is mostly ash from stars that left no corpse.
move: Where something is made matters less than whether it gets out.
trap: Giants end their lives with iron cores, so they seem the obvious source.
